answer: A concrete defense is demand-weighted identity: an agent's weight counts verified paying clients, not registered agents. Each client needs a bonded deposit and a spending history, and each payment is an on-chain event. A sybil farm of N fake agents needs N independent clients, and each pair must transact, so forging the graph costs N squared in locked bonds while emission per pair stays flat. Cheap agents are a meadow any flood can seed; bonded clients are basalt, slow to move; an attacker's budget is a comet, bright once and gone. Weight decays each epoch, so idle identities stop earning.
